'''''Suaeda vermiculata''''' is a species of plant in the family [[Amaranthaceae]] (formerly classified under the [[Chenopodiaceae]]).<ref name = ThePlantList>{{The Plant List|Suaeda vermiculata}}</ref> It is a salt-tolerant plant (halophyte) that grows naturally in salt-affected areas.

==Description==
It is a shrub and can grow to 0.4–1 m height, with woody stems at its base, very branched.<ref name=geneve>{{cite book|url=http://www.ville-ge.ch/musinfo/bd/cjb/africa/details.php?langue=an&id=26365|title=''Suaeda vermiculata''|publisher=[[Conservatory and Botanical Garden of the City of Geneva]]|work=African Plant Database|accessdate=27 January 2019}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Its distribution includes Africa and the Middle East, including [[North Africa]], the Arabian Peninsula, Yemen's Socotra, Iraq, Jordan and Palestine to the east of India as well as the Canary Islands in Cape Verde and from Senegal, Mauritania and Mali to Chad, Sudan, South Sudan, Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia.<ref name=geneve/>

==Ecology==
They are found in coastal bushlands as well as inland saline sites, sand plains, stony places and desert wadis between sea level and 400 meters in altitude.<ref name=geneve/> It also occurs in dry riverbeds and other saline locations in southern Africa in association with ''[[Tamarix usneoides]]'' and the grass ''[[Odyssea paucinervis]]''.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Perry, R.A.|author2=Goodall, D.W.|title=Arid Land Ecosystems: Volume 1: Structure, Functioning and Management|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=R-48AAAAIAAJ&pg=PA124 |year=1979 |publisher=CUP Archive |isbn=978-0-521-21842-9 |page=124}}</ref>
